_doc: Authored enrichment layer — relations a human asserts that the graph cannot derive. Schema: docs/authored-edges.md. Joined by build-graph.py; additive to edges.json (no card projects these, so the round-trip is untouched).
_types: Every edge here is kind `association` (soft, symmetric, non-gating) — build-graph stamps that. Author the `type` (the RELATION) + `basis` (the reason): `confusable` = a form/sound/sense MIX-UP to warn against (basis visual|phonetic|semantic); `cognate` = a shared ORIGIN to enrich with (basis historical|etymological|orthographic). Two ORTHOGONAL axes — a pair may carry either, both (西/襾), or neither. カ/力 confusable-only; 東/东 cognate-only. Glossary: docs/glossary.md.
_refs: between/for take a bare glyph (人 → g:人), a word surface + the entry's `audience` (可不 + cn → w:可不@cn), or an explicit node id (g:入, w:不可@cn). Every ref must resolve to a real node or the build warns and drops the entry.
_shape: `between` is an unordered SET of ≥2. build-graph emits the pairwise clique of slim links plus ONE cluster record carrying basis/note/examples — so a 3-way (己/已/巳) stores its payload once, not three times.

edges.note: The classic three-way. They differ ONLY in how far the top-left stroke closes: 开口己、半口已、闭口巳 — 'open-mouth jǐ, half-mouth yǐ, closed-mouth sì'. 己 (self) leaves a clear gap; 已 (already) closes it halfway; 巳 (6th earthly branch, the snake) seals it shut. Same three strokes, three characters.

examples.gloss: zìjǐ — oneself (己 = self; the mouth stays OPEN)
yǐjīng — already (已 = already; the mouth is HALF closed)
sìshí — the hour of the snake, 9–11am (巳 = 6th branch; the mouth is SHUT)

edges.note: Two strokes each, mirrored. In 人 (person) the two strokes MEET at the apex. In 入 (to enter) the short stroke starts partway down the long one, so the top is a CROSSING, not a clean peak — and the long stroke is the one on the right.

examples.gloss: rénrén — everyone (人 = person)
rùkǒu — entrance (入 = to enter)

edges.note: The same two characters reversed. 不可 = 'cannot / must not'. 可不 is NOT its negation: it is either the 可不可… A-not-A frame ('can or can't…?') or, colloquially, 可不(是) = emphatic agreement ('isn't it just').

examples.gloss: Isn't it just! / That's so true! — 可不(是) = emphatic agreement
(I) simply must go. — 非…不可 = 'cannot not' = must

edges.note: Same body shape. 西 (west) and the cover radical 襾 share the 西-form — 襾 is 西 with an extra horizontal stroke across the very top, and its top-only variant 覀 sits atop 要/票/覆. So a 西-looking top in those characters is the COVER radical, not 西 'west'.

examples.gloss: dōngxi — thing (lit. east-west); here 西 = west
yào — to want / important; its top is the 覀/襾 cover radical, NOT 西

edges.note: 同族 — 西 is classified under Kangxi radical 146 襾 ('cover'). Historically one radical family: 西 became the everyday character 'west', while 襾 (and its top-form 覀) is the radical 'cover' seen atop 要/票/覆. Same origin, now distinct senses — the mirror image of a confusable, which shares a look but not an origin.

Kangxi radical 80, two glyph-forms of one slot. 毋 (wú, 'do not') is the authoritative dictionary radical; 母 ('mother') is the form actually seen in the characters classed under it (每/毒/毓). Distinguished by the inner marks — 母 has two dots, 毋 a single bar — so also easily confused.

Same 母-frame, three different inner marks — tell them apart by what's inside the box: 母 (mother) keeps the two nursing dots; 毋 (wú, 'do not') strikes a single bar through them — 'don't'; 毌 (guàn, 'pass through') runs the bar clear across. A 己/已/巳-style triple.

examples.gloss: mǔqīn — mother; 母 keeps the two dots
wúyōng — no need; 毋 = 'do not', one bar through
guàn — 毌 depicts piercing-through; it survives atop 贯 (毌+贝) 'pierce / string of cash'

edges.note: The 'field with a line' family. 田 (field) is the closed grid. 由 (from / cause) is 田 with the central vertical pushing UP through the top. Its cousins extend the same stroke elsewhere: 甲 (jiǎ, first) pushes it DOWN through the bottom, 申 (shēn, to extend) through BOTH ends. Read 由 by the top-exit.

examples.gloss: zìyóu — freedom (由 = from / cause; the stroke exits the TOP)
tiándì — farmland (田 = field; the grid stays CLOSED)

edges.note: Homophones — all three read tā. 他 and 她 share the 也 phonetic and the radical carries the sense: 亻(person) → 他 'he', 女(woman) → 她 'she'. 它 (roof 宀 → 'it', for things and animals) is the same tā on a different frame; pick the character by its referent, not by the sound.

examples.gloss: tāmen — they (men / mixed group; 他 = he, person radical)
tāmen — they (all female; 她 = she, woman radical)
tāmen — they (things / animals; 它 = it, roof radical)

edges.note: Both gloss 'head'. 头 tóu is the everyday body-part word (头发, 头疼). 首 shǒu is the literary head: today it lives on as 'first / chief' (首先, 首都) and as the measure word for songs and poems (一首歌). Say 头 for your head; reach for 首 when something is the head OF a list.

examples.gloss: wǒ tóu téng — I have a headache (头 = the head you have)
shǒudū — capital city (首 = chief, the head of the list)

edges.note: Both gloss 'body', and the everyday word 身体 uses both. 身 shēn is the body as your physical self — what you carry and wear (身上, 一身). 体 tǐ leans toward form and system: 体育 (sport), 字体 (typeface), 体系 (system).

examples.gloss: wǒ shēnshang méi qián — I've no money on me (身 = one's person)
zìtǐ — typeface (体 = form, style)

edges.note: Both gloss 'not', but they negate different things. 不 bù negates a verb or adjective: not do, not be. 无 wú negates existence: 'there is none of it, without'. It is the written counterpart of 没有, and it's a common prefix (无人, 无线).

examples.gloss: wǒ bú qù — I'm not going (不 negates the verb)
wúrénjī — drone, lit. 'no-person machine' (无 = without)

edges.note: Both gloss 'from'. 从 cóng is the starting point in space or time (从北京来, 从今天起). 由 yóu is the agent or channel — 'by, through, up to': 由他决定 is 'it's his call'. When the English 'from' could be read as 'by', use 由.

examples.gloss: wǒ cóng Běijīng lái — I come from Beijing (从 = starting point)
yóu tā juédìng — it's up to him (由 = by whom)

edges.note: Both gloss 'speech'. 话 huà is the everyday noun for spoken words (说话, 电话, 中国话). 言 yán is the literary word: it survives in compounds (语言, 发言) and, as 讠, in the side of nearly every speaking character, including 话 itself.

examples.gloss: shuōhuà — to speak (话 = words, the everyday noun)
yǔyán — language (言 = speech, the literary word)

edges.note: Both gloss 'can', but for different reasons. 会 huì is a learned skill: you can because you learned how (会游泳, 会说中文). It also means 'will probably'. 可 kě is permission or possibility, and today it nearly always appears inside 可以 or 可能. (The third 'can', 能 néng, is physical ability.)

examples.gloss: wǒ huì shuō Zhōngwén — I can speak Chinese (会 = learned skill)
kěyǐ jìnlái ma — may I come in? (可 = permitted)

edges.note: Both gloss 'appearance'. 样 yàng is kind, manner, how-something-is (这样, 一样, 样子). 相 xiàng is a PERSON's looks, or a photo of them (长相, 照相). Watch the polyphone: as xiāng, 相 means 'mutually' (互相, 相信).

examples.gloss: yíyàng — the same (样 = manner, kind)
zhàoxiàng — to take a photo (相 = likeness, looks)

edges.note: Both gloss 'use', and the formal verb 使用 joins them. 用 yòng is the everyday 'use' (用筷子). On its own, 使 shǐ today mostly means 'to make or cause' someone to do or feel something: 这使我很高兴.

examples.gloss: yòng kuàizi chīfàn — eat with chopsticks (用 = use)
zhè shǐ wǒ hěn gāoxìng — this makes me very happy (使 = cause)

edges.note: Three ways to say 'and', from casual to formal. 和 hé is the everyday one, and also 'with' (我和你). 与 yǔ is its written twin, common in titles (《战争与和平》). 及 jí joins the last item of a formal list; its core sense is 'to reach', as in 来得及 'still in time'.

examples.gloss: wǒ hé nǐ — you and me (和 = everyday 'and')
Zhànzhēng yǔ Hépíng — War and Peace (与 = written 'and')
láidejí — there's still time (及 = reach)

edges.note: Both gloss 'village'. 村 cūn is the living word (农村, 村子). The village sense of 里 lǐ survives only in old compounds (邻里, 故里). Most of the time you'll meet 里 as 'inside' (这里, 家里) or as a unit of distance (公里). That 'inside' sense is not yet modelled on the card.

examples.gloss: nóngcūn — the countryside (村 = village)
línlǐ — neighbours, the neighbourhood (里 = village, old sense)

edges.note: Both gloss 'city'. 市 shì is the modern word: an administrative city (城市, 市长) and, originally, a market (超市). 邑 yì is the ancient walled town. You'll rarely see it alone, but it's everywhere as 阝 on the RIGHT of a character (都, 部, 那). The same shape on the LEFT is 阜 'mound' instead.

examples.gloss: chāoshì — supermarket (市 = market, city)
jiāoqū — the suburbs (郊 = outskirts of the town; its right-hand 阝 is 邑)

_audio: examples are voiced into /audio/sent/ by gen-audio (sent-bank). `lang` (cn|jp) picks the voice — set it per-entry or per-example; a word entry's `audience` is the fallback. audioKey is DERIVED (content-keyed off lang+text by phonetics.sentence_key) and stamped into edges.json by build-graph — never author it.
